compliance.seismic: Complies with Zone 4 earthquake requirements per GR-63, Issue 4 (Table 22)

environmental.altitude: no performance degradation up to 3048 m (10,000 ft) (Table 22)

features.macsec: IEEE 802.1AE MACsec on all Gigabit and 10 Gigabit Ethernet ports, 88 Gbps of encryption
features.optics-qsfp: the rear uplink ports take QSFP+ transceivers. The supported list is in Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool, which the guide names and which is not held here
features.optics-sfp-plus: the front uplink ports take SFP and SFP+ transceivers, singly or mixed. The supported list is in Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool, which the guide names and which is not held here
features.uplink-ports: four SFP or SFP+ ports on the front and two QSFP+ ports on the rear
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 switches. The QSFP+ ports are Virtual Chassis ports by default

management.console: RJ-45 console on the rear panel and Mini-USB Type-B console on the front, both labelled CON
management.oob: management Ethernet RJ-45 on the rear panel, with a Link/Activity lamp and a Status lamp
management.usb: one USB port on the rear panel

physical.depth-with-power-supply: 382.4 mm (15.05 in.) with a power supply installed (Table 3)
physical.weight: 4.64 kg (10.23 lb) without power supplies or fan modules (Table 3)
physical.width-with-brackets: 482 mm (19 in.) with the mounting brackets attached (Table 3)

power.power-current-max: 3 A at 100 VAC and 1.5 A at 240 VAC (Table 19)

configs.description: The switch as shipped: one 150 W AC supply in slot 0, a blank panel over slot 1 and two fan modules. Airflow is front to back.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: The back-to-front switch (Table 1) - one 150 W JPSU-150-AC-AFI supply in slot 0, a blank panel over slot 1, and two airflow-in fan modules. Air enters at the rear and leaves at the front. The front panel is the same.
configs.name: ac-afi

configs.description: The DC-powered switch (Table 1) - one 150 W JPSU-150-DC-AFO supply in slot 0 and a blank panel over slot 1. Airflow is front to back. The front panel is the same.
configs.name: dc

gaps.wanted: The front Mini-USB Type-B console, labelled CON, is drawn as decor and not placed as a port. The DCIM exporter has no route for a Mini-USB console part, and the guard test that holds every port part to the exporter fails until it has one. A change to dcim_export.py that exports a Mini-B console as a usb-mini-b console port would let the port be placed.

Which DC input rating to provision. Table 20 gives 4.7 A maximum at -48 VDC, and its note advises a 10 A breaker. The connection topic (Connecting DC Power to an EX3400 Switch) says to terminate on a source that supplies at least 7.5 A at -48 VDC. Neither rating is modelled as a figure on the supply; Table 20's 4.7 A is carried.

The EX3400-48T-DC-T1, the 1 OU ORv3 switch-tray assembly (Table 38), is not modelled. It mounts on a tray in an ORv3 rack, which is not a 19 in. rack mount, and the guide gives no drawing of its faces.
A photograph of the back-to-front power supply and fan module, to say whether their handles are a different colour from the front-to-back ones. The guide states no handle colour.

A per-port vocabulary for the Status lamp. Table 8 gives it three meanings that depend on the mode the Factory Reset/Mode button chose, so the jack keeps the component's default off, link and activity states, and the mode lamps carry the meaning.

The size of the CLEI code label and the Serial Number ID Label on the rear plate between fan 1 and power supply 0 (Figure 3 callouts 8 and 9). The plate and its corner marks are drawn as one grey rectangle.
The depth of a power supply and of a fan module. Table 3 gives a chassis depth of 350.0 mm with no supply and 382.4 mm with one, and the guide gives no dimension for the modules.
A studio photograph of the EX3400-48T rear, and a photograph of the 150 W supply. The rear is drawn from the EX3400-48P photograph.
The Junos interface names (ge-0/0/n, xe-0/2/n and the QSFP+ names). This guide names only the PIC numbers in Table 2, 0 for the RJ-45 ports, 1 for the QSFP+ ports and 2 for the SFP+ ports.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
an `attrs.performance` section; `attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 4 bays (rear 4); `physical-context` on port group rj45 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: Table 3 - height 1.72 in. (4.37 cm), width 17.4 in. (44.1 cm), or 19 in. (48.2 cm) with the mounting brackets attached, depth 13.78 in. (35 cm) with no power supply installed and 15.05 in. (38.24 cm) with one. The body of 441.0 mm is the metal between the bracket fold lines, and the 43.7 mm height is the metric figure as printed. The depth carried is the 350.0 mm of the bare chassis, and the supply adds the rest. Weight is 10.23 lb (4.64 kg) without supplies or fan modules.

color.note: photo-measured - median of the bare face between the port block and the bottom edge in the EX3400-48P front photograph, #9ea1a5, darkened to #8c9094 for the face as a whole; the uplink plate is darker (#6b6f73). The rear and the fan and supply colours are sampled the same way.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The guide's Figure 2 draws the printing too small to read, so the photograph wins for every legend. The EX3400-48T photograph prints "EX3400", with no PoE+ mark, and still prints the POE mode legend and lamp. Figure 1 and the front panel topic say the PoE lamp is present only on models with PoE, and Table 8 says it is not available without PoE. The legend and lamp are drawn as photographed, and the lamp is never lit on this model. The port numerals print light grey on this photograph, not orange as on the PoE models: #c1bcba, the median of the 20 brightest pixels in the numeral row below the jacks (193, 188, 186; the surrounding face is about 150, 152, 155). The ink is thin, so the sample is a floor on its true value.

ears.note: Mounting topics - two brackets and eight screws ship in the box and mount along the front or the rear of the side panels. The separately orderable four-post rack-mount kit holds flush and 2-in.-recess front-mounting brackets, side rails and rear blades. The recess is 2 in. (50.8 mm). The guide gives no part number for the four-post kit or for the wall-mount kit, so neither is listed under kits, and the guide's figures place the brackets without a measurable fold line, so only the recess has an `at`.

earthing.note: Table 41 - the EX3400 earthing terminal is on the rear panel, with two 10-32 screws and a two-hole lug. Figure 3 callout 4. The hole spacing is not stated in the guide; the photograph puts the two holes 16.0 mm apart. They are juniper/ex3400-ground-pair@1, two 10-32 screws on the 5/8 in. (15.875 mm) pitch of a two-hole lug, on the lighter plate that the photograph shows.

fru-bays.note: Table 2 and the guide's field-replaceable units topic - power supplies and fan modules are hot-removable and hot-insertable FRUs seated in bays, as are transceivers. The switch ships with one power supply and two fan modules (Table 36). With one supply the switch must be powered off before the supply is removed. Both fan modules must be installed for normal cooling. A supply and the fans must have the same airflow direction.

port-lamps.note: Figure 7 - each RJ-45 jack has two lamps, a Link/Activity lamp at the left corner and a Status lamp at the right corner of its keyway side. The common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 housing carries both. Figure 8 - each SFP+ uplink has a Link/Activity lamp left of its number and a Status lamp right of it. The photograph shows them as tall light-pipe slots, drawn as common/led-rect@1 turned 90. The Status lamp on a jack shows speed, duplex or enabled state according to the mode lamps, so its states are not expressible as one vocabulary here (see gaps).

port-numbering.note: The legends under each column pair read 0 and 1, then 2 and 3, up to 46 and 47, so the upper jack of a column is the even port and the lower the odd one. The guide labels the ports 0 through 47. The uplink cages are printed 0 to 3 under the cages on the front, and the rear QSFP+ ports 0 and 1. Interface names such as ge-0/0/0 are not printed on the metal and are not stated in this guide, so none is recorded.

ports.note: Table 1 and Figure 2 give 48 RJ-45 ports in four blocks of 6 columns by 2 rows, and four uplink cages. The jack and cage positions are those of the EX3400-48P, which the 48T photograph confirms to within a pixel or two: block starts 9.0 mm and a block step of 88.8 mm, the registry's 13.97 mm ganged pitch, two rows 14.0 mm apart with the upper row turned 180 so that its keyway and lamp tabs face up. The four SFP cages start at 363.7 mm and abut on the registry's 14.25 mm pitch.

power.note: Table 11 - the EX3400-48T consumes at most 120 W and has no PoE. Table 19 gives 3 A at 100 VAC and 1.5 A at 240 VAC.

rear.note: Figure 3 and the EX3400-48P rear photograph, read at 3.327 px/mm across and 3.30 px/mm down. From the left, the management corner holds the MGMT RJ-45 over a USB-A port, then the CON RJ-45, a lighter plate with two earthing holes, the earth symbol, two QSFP+ cages marked 0 and 1 with a lamp slot pair under each, and the ESD socket. Then come fan 0 at 133.7 mm and fan 1 at 182.0 mm, a label plate for the CLEI code and serial number labels, power supply slot 0 at 271.7 mm and slot 1 at 354.4 mm.

rear-modules.note: Both power supply bays are drawn at the supply's own 71.2 by 39.0 mm face, measured on slot 0 of the EX3400-48P. The blank panel in slot 1 is photographed 76.6 by 41.0 mm because it overlaps the frame of the slot, and is drawn at the supply size so that it fills the same bay. Slot 1's position is the slot 0 position plus the 82.7 mm spacing of the two numerals. The 150 W supply is drawn like the 920 W one that the photograph shows.

scale.note: Gate 1 - the front photograph is a straight-on studio shot. The face measures about 1460 px across in the 1500 px wide file. Against 441.0 mm that is 3.31 px/mm, and the right-hand block of the EX3400-48P and EX3400-48T photographs lands at the same millimetre positions (the uplink cage block starts at 363.7 and 363.9 mm), so the two faces are one design and the EX3400-48P positions are used at 3.327 px/mm. The photograph is orthographic and carries geometry. Every figure read off a picture is estimated and good to about 0.4 mm.

sources.note: EX3400 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2026-01-09 (317 pages): Tables 1 to 3, 10 to 13 and 19, Figures 1 to 4 and 7 to 10, the packing list (Table 36) and the mounting topics. Juniper image-library studio photograph ex3400-48t-front-high, straight on, which supplies the front positions. No studio photograph of the EX3400-48T rear was found, so the rear is read from the EX3400-48P rear photograph (ex3400-48p-rear-high), and the community NetBox rear elevation of the EX3400-48T was used only to confirm that the rear panel and the 150 W supply look the same. The HPE PSNow datasheet (a50014095enw) did not answer from this host, so no datasheet figure is used. The guide is copyright Juniper Networks, 2026, all rights reserved, and the studio photographs come from the maker's public image library; no terms of use are stated on the files. Nothing of either is copied here, since every face is drawn new from measurements. End of life was searched on 2026-10-21: only reseller pages for Juniper support bundles (the B-EX3400-...-E part numbers, announced 2020 and 2023) came up and no Juniper notice for the hardware, so the lifecycle is recorded as none announced.

status-block.note: Figure 5 and Table 4 give the chassis lamps SYS, ALM and MST. Figure 10 and Table 8 give the port mode lamps SPD, DX, EN and PoE and the Factory Reset/Mode button that switches them. The lamps are read off the EX3400-48P photograph at the right end (x 426.1 and 432.2 mm, y 5.0 to 18.5 step 4.5), and the 48T photograph shows the same four mode legends.
